- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.00) — reduce forecast peak values by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.00) — adjust downward bias by 1–2% to align with mean reversion.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent spikes — smooth out 3–5 day moving averages to reduce lagged overshoot.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00), forecasts should be closer to historical mean — use 18-day rolling mean as baseline.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent 7-day high to prevent artificial spikes.
- Correct for horizon mismatch: 30-day forecasts often overestimate near-term volatility — apply 10–15% downward adjustment for early horizon (1–7 days).
- If sentiment is stable and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is stable and price is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid undercorrection.
